account:
It is day 1, about 09:16. I have read today's appointment documents and am keeping morning office hours. The secretary says no new correspondence or business has arrived. I have not seen anything clearly unusual or troublesome today. Several townsfolk are on the street near town hall, but I have not heard what brings them here and cannot infer their purpose.

Today's business includes a grain inspection at the east-bank mill at ten, lunch at home at noon, council letters at the office at thirteen, and tea with my neighbour at the dockside cottage at fifteen. I am due back at the office at sixteen thirty. The additional engagement is with the innkeeper: he has confirmed that he will meet me at my office at seventeen forty-five, then accompany me to the great hall for an eighteen hundred meeting about the inn's service to town. The secretary recorded this in an approved supplement, leaving the original appointments unchanged. As far as I know, this is ordinary planned town business; I have no evidence of another purpose or an unusual gathering.
